page: Amazon Web Services m8a.8xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the AMD EPYC 9R45 processor on the x86_64 architecture, managed by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The instance features 32 dedicated physical cores with a single thread per core, operating at clock frequencies up to 4.5 GHz. It includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 128.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory clocked at 6 GHz, establishing a standard 1:4 core-to-memory allocation of 4.0 GB per core. The server configuration includes no bundled local NVMe storage and no discrete GPUs, utilizing network-attached storage via a 15 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Benchmark results place the m8a.8xlarge in the top tier for single-core and multi-core compute throughput, recording a Geekbench single-core score of 2816.0 and a multi-core score of 28042.0. Memory throughput reaches 213.23 GB/sec in large-block uncached reads and 136.6 GB/sec in uncached writes. Hardware support includes AVX-512 vector extensions with VNNI and BF16, facilitating strong results in compression (41.41 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip) and PassMark database operations (40843.98). While CPU-based lightweight LLM inference reaches 5311.83 tokens/sec on 135M prompt processing, throughput scales down to average tier on 70B models due to the absence of dedicated matrix hardware accelerators.

The 1:1 physical core-to-thread ratio provides predictable execution times without the thread contention typical of simultaneous multithreading. Cost efficiency is characterized by high resource density and robust compute throughput per core, though workloads requiring heavy local I/O must account for external network storage constraints over the 15 Gbps interface. The instance is structured for general enterprise deployments, relational and in-memory databases, continuous integration build pipelines, and high-concurrency web serving.
description: Amazon Web Services m8a.8xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance powered by a 4.5 GHz AMD EPYC 9R45 processor with 32 dedicated physical cores, 32 vCPUs, and 128 GB of DDR5 memory running at 6 GHz. Based on the AWS Nitro System with x86_64 architecture, the instance provides 15 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, while omitting bundled local storage and discrete GPUs. In benchmark testing, the m8a.8xlarge exhibits top-tier single-core and multi-core metrics, achieving high scores in Geekbench, PassMark database operations, and uncached memory bandwidth exceeding 213 GB/sec. Support for AVX-512, VNNI, and BF16 enables fast vector processing and CPU-based lightweight machine learning inference. With its balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio and absence of SMT contention, this instance is well suited for enterprise application servers, relational databases, code compilation suites, and multi-threaded data processing tasks.
